knowledge_gaps: Reproducibility requires exact panel sizes, prefix cutoffs, candidate counts, full-history exclusion rules, TF-IDF settings, similarity thresholds, age bins, shuffle repetitions, tie handling, and rank-statistic definitions.

The scoring adapter remains unspecified: existing hooks score per-position candidates, whereas the proposed probe needs final-valid-position scoring over arbitrary candidate sets. Category-local item IDs and separately trained model routing also need explicit handling.

Compacted deletion changes history length, positional encodings, and potentially the final event together. Matched deletion counts alone cannot isolate recency or semantic repetition effects. TF-IDF groups may reproduce the surface-similarity shortcuts identified in the feedback.

Sensitivity has no established beneficial direction or demonstrated relationship to validation HR@10. The potential score of 8 is speculative, while difficulty 3 understates control construction and adapter verification. Sampled diagnostic rankings also cannot replace the required full-catalog recommendations for twenty training users.

Diagnostics must preserve random-number-generator and loader state as well as model mode, so running them does not change subsequent training. Computational limits and safeguards against repeatedly adapting to the same validation users are unspecified.

follow_up_queries.reason: Identify controls that separate information removal from positional artifacts, and assess whether lexical repetition groups measure more than shared terminology.
follow_up_queries.query: In SASRec sequential recommendation, what experimental controls distinguish recency and semantic-history dependence from sequence-length, positional-encoding, and last-item effects when comparing compacted deletions, masking, and last-item-fixed shuffling? Include methods for validating TF-IDF title/description groups and matching deletion controls on interaction age.

follow_up_queries.reason: Resolve implementation details needed for faithful, reproducible diagnostics without changing subsequent training.
follow_up_queries.query: How should a deterministic SASRec history-perturbation diagnostic implement final-valid-position candidate scoring, left padding, maximum-length truncation, unseen-item exclusion, score ties, and independent random generators? Include preserving PyTorch model modes, RNG state, and DataLoader sampling state during diagnostic inference.

follow_up_queries.reason: Establish whether diagnostic sensitivity can guide useful changes and how to avoid overstating evidence from a small, repeatedly inspected panel.
follow_up_queries.query: What research validates sequential-recommender history-perturbation sensitivity against held-out ranking improvements? Consider controlled faults, identity-edit controls, repeated perturbations, paired user uncertainty estimates, sampled versus full-catalog rankings, and adaptive validation overfitting when selecting models by macro HR@10 across four Amazon datasets.
